name: Vomp
kurzbeschreibung: A charming residential community in the Unterinntal valley, featuring a stunning Baroque church and breathtaking views of the Tuxer Alpen.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The market town of Vomp is situated at an elevation of 566 metres above sea level in the Lower Inn Valley north of the River Inn, directly opposite the historic district capital of Schwaz. With approximately 5,400 inhabitants and an extraordinary municipal territory spanning more than 182 square kilometres, Vomp is the second-largest municipality in the Schwaz district and one of the largest in Tyrol. The area extends from the sunny valley floor across the Vomper plateau deep into the Karwendel Nature Park, reaching the dramatic Laliderer walls and the Bavarian border. Consequently, Vomp encompasses world-famous alpine landscapes such as the Riss Valley with Hinterriss and the Grosser Ahornboden in the Eng. Vomp uniquely combines an active commercial and residential hub in the valley with pristine, high-alpine wilderness in the Karwendel.

Geschichte

Settlement in the area traces back to pre-Christian times, corroborated by archaeological discoveries from the Bronze and Iron Ages. The village was first documented around 930 AD under the name 'Fonapa', a pre-Roman Celtic term referring to bubbling springs and watercourses. During the Middle Ages, Vomp served as an influential primary parish in the Inn Valley responsible for surrounding hamlets. The Benedictine Abbey of St. Georgenberg-Fiecht played a pivotal historic role: after devastating fires repeatedly ravaged the mountain monastery of St. Georgenberg, a magnificent Baroque abbey complex was constructed in Fiecht during the 18th century. In 1470, Archduke Sigismund of Austria founded Schloss Sigmundslust, which later housed one of Tyrol's earliest printing presses. The late Gothic parish church dedicated to Saints Peter and Paul was extensively renovated in the 19th century following an 1809 fire.

Anreise

In the valley, Vomp benefits from first-rate transport infrastructure within central Tyrol. Motorists reach the village directly via the Inntal Autobahn A12 exiting at Schwaz or Vomp, or toll-free along the federal highway B171. Rail travelers enjoy frequent connections on the Lower Inn Valley railway line: the S-Bahn Tirol serves the Vomp railway stop every 30 minutes with direct links to Innsbruck and Kufstein, while the nearby express railway station in Jenbach provides international train connections. Regional buses seamlessly link the village centre to surrounding communities. The northern territory around Hinterriss and the Grosser Ahornboden is accessible by road via Upper Bavaria through Vorderriss.

Tipps

A premier alpine highlight is the Grosser Ahornboden in the Eng in the Karwendel, where more than 2,000 ancient sycamore maple trees framed by towering limestone cliffs create an awe-inspiring natural sanctuary, particularly enchanting during autumn. Culture enthusiasts should tour Stift Fiecht with its majestic Baroque church and embark on a scenic hike to Tyrol's oldest pilgrimage site at St. Georgenberg. For mountain hikers, the rugged Vomper Loch gorge offers wild alpine paths, while Binsalm and the Lamsenjoch hut are celebrated destinations for mountaineering. Cyclists can enjoy leisurely family rides along the riverside Inn Cycle Path.
